judgments.justification: “improved average BLEU by 3.1 points…from 12.0 to 15.1…across the four low-resource pairs” reports the finding.
“a smaller gain than the 5.8-point average improvement…reported…by Rasmussen-Obi & Petrakis” gives the correct direction and attribution.
The passage does not report per-pair BLEU gains over genuine-only training; its every-pair claim concerns comparison with unfiltered back-translation.
The passage compares filtered chrF with unfiltered chrF, not with the genuine-only average of 39.0.
“outperformed unfiltered back-translation on average BLEU (15.1 vs 13.4) and average chrF (42.3 vs 40.3)” reports both advantages.
It does not mention single-run training, missing statistical tests, or the descriptive nature of the comparisons.
Although it uses Rasmussen-Obi and Petrakis, it does not discuss Ambergate and Toivonen or P1’s failure to support the roughly six-point claim.
It does not report P2’s 2.9-point unfiltered gain or explicitly compare that result with Wickersham-MT’s 1.4-point unfiltered gain.
“improved average BLEU by 3.1 points…from 12.0 to 15.1” correctly reports Wickersham-MT’s filtered gain over genuine-only data.
“3.1 points…a smaller gain than the 5.8-point average improvement…by Rasmussen-Obi & Petrakis” correctly relates and attributes the gains.
